title: The Seller's Standing Record in Seller Performance Standing
content:
**Rule.** A seller has exactly one standing record; every order, defect and violation of the seller is booked to it.

A Seller Performance Standing record is opened when the seller first lists. The number of standing records a seller may hold is 1.

## Retired clause

> A closed record does not count, so a seller who closed voluntarily and returns gets a new record.

This clause is **no longer in force**. It has been superseded by the current basis and is shown here only so that the record of the rule is complete; it is not applied.

## What the rule settles

| Question | Answer under the rule in force |
|---|---|
| How many standing records may one seller hold? | 1 |
| To which record are the seller's orders booked? | The seller's one standing record |
| To which record are the seller's defects and violations booked? | The same record |

**Hypothetical example.** A seller with orders on several listings has a single Seller Performance Standing record; the orders, any defects on them and any policy violations against any of those listings are all booked to that one record.

superseded_clauses: A closed record does not count, so a seller who closed voluntarily and returns gets a new record.
